reference: GNU coreutils touch and file-scoped GNU sync -d provide direct parity oracles for those two operations. bashio's descriptor-based random-access API has no matching GNU CLI, so its cases are contracts based on the documented interface and POSIX pread/pwrite/lseek/fstat/ftruncate semantics; expected hex bytes are independently calculated from literal fixture data. Bash type/help metadata is checked as a contract. Ownership and network configuration are deferred.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
GNU touch parity for existing-file preservation and missing-file creation
Open creation, exclusive creation, truncation modes, and FD variable binding
Binary pread/pwrite, lowercase hex output, positional offset independence, and EOF behavior
lseek set/current positions and fstat size/mode fields
exclusions: bashio chown is deferred because ownership changes are prohibited in this fixture run.
bashio set-addr and set-route are deferred because network configuration must not be attempted.
The harness tree snapshot does not include timestamps, so touch mtime changes are not asserted.
No device paths, external network targets, or host/system state are used.

cases.purpose: The candidate registers bashio as a Bash builtin, as required for the loadable interface.
Bash help must resolve the loadable's documented usage; the check requires nonempty help text without asserting presentation formatting.
Checks binary-safe hex reads and writes, lseek set/current results, and the POSIX guarantee that pread and pwrite leave the descriptor's current offset unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'abcdef' > sample.bin
bashio open sample.bin r+ fd
bashio lseek "$fd" 3 set
bashio pread "$fd" 4 1 -x
bashio lseek "$fd" 0 cur
bashio pwrite "$fd" 414200ff 2
bashio lseek "$fd" 0 cur
bashio pread "$fd" 6 0 -x
bashio close "$fd"

cases.purpose: Checks w+ truncation, r+ creation with -c -x, FD variable binding, fstat size and octal mode, pwrite/readback, and EEXIST failure on a second exclusive create. The changing mtime field is checked for integer form but omitted from cross-run output.
cases.script:
umask 022
printf 'obsolete' > trunc.bin
bashio open trunc.bin w+ fd
meta=$(bashio fstat "$fd")
read -r size mtime mode <<< "$meta"
[[ $size == 0 && $mtime =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $mode == 644 ]]
printf '%s %s\n' "$size" "$mode"
bashio close "$fd"
bashio open fresh.bin r+ -c -x fd
bashio pwrite "$fd" 515253 0
meta=$(bashio fstat "$fd")
read -r size mtime mode <<< "$meta"
[[ $size == 3 && $mtime =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $mode == 644 ]]
printf '%s %s\n' "$size" "$mode"
bashio pread "$fd" 3 0 -x
bashio close "$fd"
set +e
bashio open fresh.bin r+ -c -x duplicate
rc=$?
set -e
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'collision=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Checks descriptor truncation both downward and upward, fstat's resulting size field, and zero-filled bytes in the extension.
cases.script:
printf '0123456789' > sample.bin
bashio open sample.bin r+ fd
bashio truncate "$fd" 4
meta=$(bashio fstat "$fd")
read -r size mtime mode <<< "$meta"
[[ $size == 4 && $mtime =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
printf '%s\n' "$size"
bashio truncate "$fd" 7
bashio pread "$fd" 7 0 -x
bashio close "$fd"

cases.purpose: Covers zero-length pread (no bytes emitted), a positive-length short read at EOF, and a positive-length hex read starting at EOF.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > sample.bin
bashio open sample.bin r fd
bashio pread "$fd" 0 0 -x
printf '|'
bashio pread "$fd" 5 2 -x
printf '|'
bashio pread "$fd" 3 3 -x
bashio close "$fd"

cases.purpose: Compares bashio touch with GNU touch for preserving an existing file and creating a missing empty file. The runner compares resulting file bytes and modes; it does not snapshot timestamps.
cases.script:
candidate=0
if [[ $(type -t bashio) == builtin ]]; then candidate=1; fi
printf 'kept\n' > existing.txt
if (( candidate )); then
  bashio touch existing.txt created.txt
else
  touch existing.txt created.txt
fi
[[ -f existing.txt && -f created.txt && $(<existing.txt) == kept && ! -s created.txt ]]
printf 'touch-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Compares bashio sync on an open private fixture file with GNU coreutils sync -d on that same relative file; no system-wide sync operation is used.
cases.script:
candidate=0
if [[ $(type -t bashio) == builtin ]]; then candidate=1; fi
printf 'private fixture data\n' > sync.bin
if (( candidate )); then
  bashio open sync.bin r+ fd
  bashio sync "$fd"
  bashio close "$fd"
else
  sync -d sync.bin
fi
printf 'sync-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Ownership changes are outside the permitted fixture operations for this run.
cases.reason: No bashio chown invocation has executed in any run. Identity-preserving and parsing/symlink obligations are reachable by the existing legacy runner; only distinct-id transfer needs CAP_CHOWN plus synthetic identities.

bashio pread "$fd" 5 0
bashio close "$fd"
